title: autotune: default batching/caching and quantization profiles + unit-econ tooling
author: Sara Li
description: Motivation: reduce per-token unit cost and make cost/perf defaults easier to adopt across hosted and dedicated deployments by providing automated defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching plus a small set of validated quantization profiles; also ship a lightweight unit-economics (uecon) CLI and DB table to make impact visible to product/infra teams. Summary: this PR adds an autotune heuristics module that computes default batching window and cache retention settings based on recent request latency and token distributions; introduces three quantization profiles (fp16, int8-q4, int4-q3) with hardware hints and fallback chains; ships a uecon service and CLI to ingest runtime metrics and compute per-route/unit token cost and projected savings for suggested optimizations. Key points: non-breaking defaults (feature gated, opt-in by org via /settings/autotune); rollout strategy includes a 10% canary then gradual ramp with automatic rollback on regression; added telemetry (histograms + per-model profiles) and eval hooks to ensure output quality remains within tolerance for quantized variants. Checklist: - [x] autotune heuristics implementation - [x] quant profiles and model metadata - [x] uecon DB migration and simple CLI - [x] tests for decision logic and basic e2e smoke - [x] docs and admin console toggle - [x] perf benchmark reproducible scripts Related tickets: ENG-4211, ENG-4332, PM-158 This description includes implementation notes, tests, rollout, and monitoring guidance.

review_comments: Asha Patel: High-level looks good. Please confirm that quantization profiles include fallback chains when model quality regresses and that those rollbacks are observable in uecon.
Sara Li: Confirmed. profiles.yaml includes explicit fallback_order and we emit quality_regression events to the uecon ingest endpoint so the console can surface degraded ROUGE/EM/LL differences.
Miguel Santos: Minor: caching retention default of 300s seems high for low-latency routes. Suggest 60s for routes with p95 < 100ms.
Sara Li: Updated heuristics to clamp retention based on latency buckets; added unit test covering the clamp behavior.
Ethan Cho: CI flaky tests were blocking; I left a comment to isolate the external-timing dependency. We should ensure perf-gate workflow doesn't block merges for non-critical paths.
Sara Li: I've moved the benchmark gating to a separate workflow that runs post-merge for now and kept the canary perf checks in CI to prevent regressions on main.
Priya Raman: Can you add a brief admin-console screenshot and a one-line explainer for SRE runbook?

Asha Patel: Approved after addressing comments.
release_notes: Add autotune defaults for batching and prefix/KV caching; introduce three validated quantization profiles and a unit-econ service/CLI to estimate per-route token costs and projected savings. Feature gated and rolled out via canary.
rollout_plan: canary 10% traffic for 48h with automatic rollback on latency or quality regression; then 50% for 24h; then org-wide opt-in. Admin console toggle and logs available under Console -> Performance -> Autotune.
observability_notes: Emits telemetry: autotune.decisions{model,route}, quant.fallbacks{model,profile}, uecon.cost_estimate{route}; add Grafana dashboard autotune/uecon-summary and an alert on regression >5% p95 latency or >2% quality metric delta for quantized variants.
manual_steps: DB migration: tools/uecon/migrations/0002_create_unit_econ.sql; run alembic upgrade head on uecon DB; enable autotune in admin console per-org; run benchmarks/./canary_run.sh to validate throughput on dedicated pools.
notes: This PR intentionally keeps safe defaults behind a feature flag; we expect follow-ups to expand profile coverage and add per-tenant heuristics. Benchmarks attached reproduce ~12-18% token cost improvement for chat read-heavy workloads and ~4-8% for generation-heavy workloads depending on model and hardware.
external_impact: No user-facing API changes; operator-only defaults and new admin tooling. Customers using pinned model profiles will not be affected until they enable autotune.
